# Contextory

## Project memory for native agents

Contextory connects requests, specifications, source code, decisions and verification evidence in a local project ledger. Work in the native Codex, Claude Code or IBM Bob chat, then use Contextory to recover what was requested, what changed and why.

This guide describes Contextory 0.11.0, a preview qualified on Windows with trusted local folders in VS Code and IBM Bob. The extension needs Node.js 24+. Python 3.10+ is optional for Python analysis. Your agent supplies its own account, model and conversation.

[Install Contextory](install.md)

[Complete your first tracked change](quickstart.md)

## Find your next step

| Goal | Guide |

| Integrate another client | Adaptation, CLI and MCP API |

[Explore the interface](walkthroughs.md)

[Read MCP contracts](api.md)

## From request to verified result

1. Describe an authorized change in native chat. Recover earlier decisions and inspect current source.
2. Review a request split into milestones and specifications with clear acceptance criteria.
3. Keep findings, decisions and independent check results attached to each specification.
4. Confirm explicit completion and export a report that explains the final result.

[Write a useful implementation outcome](outcomes.md)

## Project explanations

Use Tools > Documentation to find explanations linked to current source and tracked work. The bundled documentation/Carbon capability requires no external plugin; generation runs on demand.

[Read the project documentation guide](documentation.md)

# Installation and upgrades

## Check your environment

| Requirement | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Windows; trusted local project folders | Qualified editor environment, including up to 16 non-nested folders |
| VS Code 1.96+ or IBM Bob | Extension host; published checks used VS Code 1.145.3 and Bob API 1.126.0 |
| Node.js 24+ | Runs the isolated service with node:sqlite |
| A separately installed native agent | Codex, Claude Code or IBM Bob chat and authentication |
| Python 3.10+ (optional) | Parses Python source and source flow |

Check installed runtimes

```powershell
node --version
python --version
```

## Install the VSIX

1. Download contextory-workspace-0.11.0.vsix and its .sha256 from the v0.11.0 GitHub release.
2. Compare the package SHA-256 with the accompanying checksum.
3. In Extensions, open the … menu, select Install from VSIX… and choose the downloaded file. Reload if prompted.
4. Open a trusted local project. The service and configured startup agents prepare in the background; open Contextory whenever you want to inspect work. The initial project has no requests.

[Download version 0.11.0](https://github.com/igormicadei/Contextory/releases/tag/v0.11.0)

Verify and install the release package

```powershell
(Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 .\contextory-workspace-0.11.0.vsix).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
Get-Content .\contextory-workspace-0.11.0.sha256
code --install-extension .\contextory-workspace-0.11.0.vsix
```

End users do not need npm, Rust, a database server or an embedding model. Install and sign in to the native agent through its own interface. Restart the editor after installing Node if its PATH has not refreshed.

## Upgrade, disconnect or uninstall

- To upgrade the same extension identity, install the newer VSIX, reload the editor and reload the native MCP session. Existing project records stay in editor-managed storage.
- To remove a bridge, click its green footer control or run Contextory: Disconnect an Agent. Only owned entries are removed. Use the command for a configured bridge whose light is gray.
- Before uninstalling, disconnect agents and back up the project ledger. Uninstall through Extensions; remove storage only after retaining the records you need.
- Older builds under the previous product identity keep records in their original storage; automatic import is unavailable. Disconnect the old build before replacing it.

[Storage and configuration reference](reference.md)

- package.json

- src/providers/clients.ts

# Your first tracked change

## Connect your native agent

1. Open the trusted project. Contextory starts the service and prepares detected supported agents when Auto-connect is on, without needing to display its sidebar.
2. For manual setup, click the agent footer control or run Contextory: Connect Native Codex, Contextory: Connect Native Claude Code or Contextory: Connect Native IBM Bob.
3. Review the generated workspace configuration and approve MCP/hooks through the native client. Reload or reopen that session when requested.
4. Ask the agent to call contextory_workspace_get and contextory_context_get. A green footer light records observed MCP traffic in the current service.

![Contextory sidebar with request progress and native agent controls.](../assets/companion-sidebar.png)

Contextory sidebar captured from the application; records are examples.

> A configured bridge or an Extension Host restart does not grant native hook trust. The light reports traffic, not agent sign-in or successful execution of every hook.

## Configure one meaningful check

Open Preferences: Open Workspace Settings (JSON). Add a recipe for an existing project command. The example suits a project that uses Node’s built-in test runner; adapt its executable, arguments and timeout to your project.

Workspace check recipe

```json
{
  "contextory.checks": [{
    "id": "unit", "name": "Unit tests",
    "executable": "node", "args": ["--test"], "timeoutMs": 120000
  }]
}
```

Recipes execute trusted workspace code with an executable and argument array. MCP calls select the recipe by ID and do not supply arbitrary shell commands.

## Implement and complete a specification

Example request for native chat

```text
Use Contextory to track this change: add retry handling to checkout. Recover earlier decisions, create milestones and specs with acceptance criteria, inspect the affected source, record findings and decisions, run our configured checks and explicitly complete each verified spec.
```

1. Review the request and acceptance criteria in Requests. The agent attaches its session and claims a specification lease before recording implementation work.
2. Inspect the changes, findings, decisions and check results under the selected specification.
3. The agent submits an outcome with evidence for every criterion, then calls contextory_spec_change with action=complete and the returned revision.
4. Confirm completed status. A submission alone leaves work open. Export the request report to review the durable record.

![Request list beside the selected specification.](../assets/panel-requests.png)

Requests in a horizontal editor Panel.

[Resolve an open or submitted spec](troubleshooting.md)

# What Contextory provides

## Choose a capability

| Capability | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Requests, milestones and specifications | Original intent, acceptance criteria, dependencies, revisions and verified completion |
| Project memory | Findings, fixes, choices, alternatives, evidence and outcome reports |
| Workspace projects | Separate records and source graphs; linked requests across explicitly selected folders |
| Architecture and Code map | Source navigation, subsystem dependencies, task context and bounded call/branch flow |
| Governed Knowledge | File responsibilities, rule/feature/test links and UI interaction definitions with human review |
| Versions | Repository-wide Git observation, release plans, local tags and separately authorized publication |
| Search and reports | Lexical search, optional local semantic retrieval, paged history and request exports |
| Native and portable integrations | Codex/Claude/Bob adapters, shared skills, generic MCP and standalone CLI |

[Follow the UI walkthroughs](walkthroughs.md)

[Use advanced source and workspace workflows](advanced.md)

## Read results with their limits

1. Select the owning Project before inspecting records. Preserve project identity when copying citations or exporting results.
2. Read coverage, freshness and truncation notices beside source results. Refine the scope or follow pagination before drawing conclusions.
3. Use independently executed checks to verify a specification. Indexed test references and source diagrams describe possible relationships.

![Subsystem map, repository explorer and source inspector.](../assets/architecture-explorer.png)

Architecture explorer captured from Contextory.

# Interface walkthroughs

## Work and Requests

1. Open Contextory and select the owning Project. Work shows the current specification, recorded criterion evidence, running checks, blockers and latest meaningful work. An empty project offers a new request.
2. Choose Requests and + New request. Enter Title and What should change?, select affected projects when needed, then Create request. Open one request to inspect its plan; expand its brief and actions only when needed.
3. Expand a milestone, select its spec and open Specification details for the plan, issues, decisions, evidence, outcome, usage or history. The evidence counts describe recorded verification; they do not estimate time remaining.
4. Use Tools for Knowledge, Versions, History, Code map and Architecture. Request exports and relationship links remain available in the selected request or specification.

![Request list beside the selected specification.](../assets/panel-requests.png)

Requests in a horizontal editor Panel.

While a project switches, the UI shows Switching project and ignores replies from the previous project. Switching projects clears unfinished form drafts. During an operation, a progress indicator and status notice report activity or failure.

## Inspect architecture and source flow

1. Open Tools > Architecture or run Contextory: Explore Architecture. Select a subsystem, file and symbol in the coordinated map, tree and inspector.
2. Use Explore connections and the relationship/direction filters. Matrix rows depend on columns; a reciprocal marker identifies direct dependencies in both directions.
3. For detailed flow, place the editor cursor in a source function and run Contextory: Trace Flow from Here, or use Code map. Select a step to inspect calls, branches and source.
4. Use zoom, Fit, background drag and source buttons. If no indexed connections appear, choose another scope or Refresh code index and review coverage notices.

![Subsystem map, repository explorer and source inspector.](../assets/architecture-explorer.png)

Architecture explorer captured from Contextory.

![Flow steps, directed diagram and source inspector.](../assets/code-map-explorer.png)

Bounded source-flow explorer in Contextory.

## Use Approvals, Knowledge and Versions

1. Open the Approvals tab or the review alert to review pending items. The tab shows a pending count and contains no already-reviewed definitions. Use Tools > Knowledge for definition search and source coverage.
2. Read the agent’s plain-language explanation. Approve or Reject needs no comment; write instructions only when requesting changes. Source snapshots update automatically, and replies return to the linked conversation through trusted hooks. Use Reopen conversation when the native session has stopped.
3. Open Tools > Versions to inspect the current version, commits and release plans. Review version, files and changelog before applying; Publish is a separately authorized release action.

![Project versions and release details in the editor Panel.](../assets/panel-versions.png)

Versions captured from the application.

[Understand definition review and source freshness](knowledge.md)

[Understand release planning and publication](releases.md)

## History, layout and keyboard use

1. Open Tools > History, or the selected request/specification history. Filter its scope and use Load older activity to page earlier events.
2. To use the horizontal layout, move Workspace Tasks to the editor Panel and resize it. Wide, short views place the request list beside the specification inspector.
3. Use Tab to reach controls, Enter or Space to activate map nodes, arrow keys on focused canvases and Ctrl+wheel to zoom. The interface follows the current editor theme and high-contrast colors.

![History filters and chronological audit events.](../assets/panel-history.png)

Project history in the editor Panel.

Resizing or docking preserves selection, drafts, expanded details and scroll within the same project. Narrow sidebars stack work and details; wide, shallow panels split them. Loading, errors and retained last-received data stay explicit. Screenshots show the production webview with isolated example records, not an authenticated native-agent chat.

# Daily user guide

## Multiple projects in one workspace

Open up to 16 trusted local, non-nested folders. The Project selector scopes Requests, Approvals, Knowledge, History, Versions and Architecture. Records, checks, evidence, source graphs, reference repositories and releases belong to each project independently. Removing a folder detaches it while retaining its storage.

1. In New request, select every affected project. Each selected project receives its own linked local request.
2. Inspect Across projects for branch status. Each branch needs its own milestones, specs, lease, checks and completed outcome.
3. If creation partially succeeds, use Retry missing branches on the original owner. Retain the original operation ID and inputs in agent automation. Missing or offline branches keep the group incomplete.

![Request list beside the selected specification.](../assets/panel-requests.png)

Requests in a horizontal editor Panel.

## Prepare connections at startup

Service startup and native bridge preparation run when the extension activates, even while Explorer or another sidebar is visible. Trust, folder, installed-agent and repaired runtime changes enter the same recovery path. Auto-connect pauses remain respected.

Auto-connect defaults to on and contextory.startupAgent defaults to auto, preparing all detected supported agents. Use the footer Auto-connect switch to pause automatic setup. Existing connections, sessions and records remain available. A manually disconnected provider stays opted out until reconnected.

Startup choices are auto, last-used, codex, claude, bob and none. Contextory prepares workspace-local configuration; native clients control trust, MCP reload, sign-in and session startup.

![Contextory sidebar with request progress and native agent controls.](../assets/companion-sidebar.png)

Contextory sidebar captured from the application; records are examples.

## Configure checks

Example workspace recipe

```json
{
  "contextory.checks": [{
    "id": "unit", "name": "Unit tests",
    "executable": "node", "args": ["--test"], "timeoutMs": 120000
  }]
}
```

Use executable plus argument arrays for real project checks. The agent invokes a configured recipe, polls its job and maps independently produced evidence to each current criterion. Source, contract or attempt changes can invalidate older evidence.

Configure up to 256 recipes. Invalid settings show Fix check settings while keeping the service connection and last valid recipe list. A fresh service has no valid recipes until configuration succeeds.

## Read model and usage records

The Usage section in Specification details and contextory_usage_get show observed metadata. Codex can report per-request token counts, Claude provides model metadata, and Bob’s documented hooks currently supply neither. Missing counts remain unavailable. Session/lease correlation is exact; unassigned observations remain unassigned.

Counts are not billing or quota estimates. Cached and reasoning tokens are subsets. Contextory does not read or mirror native conversations to calculate usage.

## Recover a connection or existing chat

1. Keep the project editor open and run Contextory: Check Native Connections. Read current-service MCP and hook observations in Output > Contextory.
2. Ask the existing agent to rediscover its advertised tools and make a read-only workspace/context call. If tools are missing, use Contextory: Restart Agent Extensions and reopen the chat as needed.
3. For missing or stale hooks, use Rebuild hooks in the footer or Contextory: Rebuild Agent Hooks. Select the project/provider, inspect repaired files and review native hook trust.
4. After one unchanged repair, inspect native trust and service logs. Repeating repairs cannot approve hooks. On Codex, /hooks approvals can differ for C: and c: path casing.

The proxy keeps discovery available during delayed startup and retries readiness for up to five minutes, with foreground waits bounded to 15 seconds. It rereads descriptors after restarts and never automatically replays a dispatched mutation. A contract mismatch needs the displayed reload/restart action.

## Project explanations

Use Tools > Documentation to find explanations linked to current source and tracked work. The bundled documentation/Carbon capability requires no external plugin; generation runs on demand.

[Read the project documentation guide](documentation.md)

## Follow the VS Code display language

Contextory follows the editor's display language for built-in labels, command titles, settings descriptions, native dialogs and webview controls. English and Brazilian Portuguese are supported. pt/pt-br select pt-BR; other unsupported locales fall back to English. The sidebar, horizontal panel, architecture, source flow and relationships share the same locale, including accessibility labels and dates.

1. Use VS Code's Configure Display Language command and choose English or Brazilian Portuguese. Install the language pack through VS Code if needed, then restart as requested by the editor.
2. Open Contextory. New webview documents take vscode.env.language, and the editor configures that normalized language for every connected project.
3. Ask the agent to read contextory_context_get. uiLanguage and contentLanguageInstruction tell it to write every new UI-facing record in the editor language, even when the conversation uses another language.

Existing requests, definitions, decisions, reports and source identifiers keep their original text. Localization translates source-owned interface messages before dynamic values are inserted; it never rewrites stored prose, code, paths, IDs or tool keys. Raw code/command output and unknown diagnostics retain their original language. Change language in VS Code and reload; Contextory has no competing language preference.

![Portuguese Contextory interface around original English project entries](../assets/knowledge-pt-BR.png)

Built-in controls follow Brazilian Portuguese; stored sample definitions remain exactly as authored.

The project's language is set only through authenticated editor configuration and persists in that project's service storage. Standalone/headless projects default to English; attaching to an editor-managed ledger retains its last configured language. Native hooks repeat the content-language instruction after session starts and before tools, including pending-review responses. This is an instruction to the native agent, not a language detector or automatic translation of its output.

# Code intelligence and advanced workflows

## Retrieve current task context

1. Start with contextory_workspace_get, then pass the intended projectId on every related call. UI selection never changes an agent server’s local default.
2. Call contextory_code_context_get with the actual task, known paths and a bounded budgetTokens value. Read the cited current source.
3. Use architecture for orientation, impact for dependencies/callers, path for connections, and flow trace for detailed calls/branches. Use search for earlier decisions and inspect their current state and revision.
4. Re-query relevant source after saved changes. Saved-file graphs refresh automatically; unsaved editor flow overlays remain separate. Page or narrow truncated results.

![Subsystem map, repository explorer and source inspector.](../assets/architecture-explorer.png)

Architecture explorer captured from Contextory.

Task-context arguments; replace the project ID

```json
{ "projectId": "PROJECT-ID", "query": "How are retries bounded?", "paths": ["src"], "budgetTokens": 3000 }
```

Qualify ambiguous definitions as source:path#qualifiedName. Task context accepts 512–6000 estimated tokens and caps JSON UTF-8 bytes at three times the estimate. Graph links and test references do not establish observed execution or complete behavioral coverage.

## Compare a reference repository

1. In Architecture, choose Add reference and select an authorized absolute local directory. Up to eight references can be registered per project.
2. Choose that Codebase, or pass its returned codebaseId on source/flow calls. Keep its identity and root with every citation.
3. Detach reference removes the registration while preserving source files. Registration and inspection do not authorize implementation in either repository.

Inspect an explicitly chosen reference

```powershell
node dist/contextory.mjs reference-add C:/Sources/LegacyApp --root C:/Projects/NewApp --name "Legacy app"
node dist/contextory.mjs references --root C:/Projects/NewApp
node dist/contextory.mjs architecture --root C:/Projects/NewApp --codebase ref-ID
```

Use actual returned IDs. References have separate source projections, refresh on queries and exclude the active project’s work records. Missing roots fail explicitly. Reference search is lexical; semantic-only mode is unavailable.

## Configure extraction and coverage

Optional contextory.project.json

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1, "name": "Checkout",
  "include": ["src/**", "tests/**", "docs/**", "*.json"],
  "exclude": ["src/generated/**"], "entryPoints": ["src/main.ts"],
  "maxFiles": 2000, "maxBytes": 16777216
}
```

TypeScript/JavaScript uses the TypeScript compiler; Python uses isolated AST parsing without importing workspace modules. Dynamic dispatch, framework injection, dependency implementation and unsupported languages remain gaps. The default input budget is 2,000 files/16 MiB, up to 512 KiB per file; configurable limits reach 10,000 files/64 MiB. Extraction caps and truncation are reported.

## Import optional Graphify data

Refresh/import arguments

```json
{ "graphifyPath": "graphify-out/graph.json" }
```

Pass these arguments to contextory_code_index_refresh. The importer checks schema, bounded JSON, IDs, edge endpoints and included local source paths; failures preserve the previous import. Regenerate and re-import the entire graph when a cited source changes, disappears or is excluded. Graphify is optional and its provenance/accuracy limits remain visible.

Use Tools > Documentation to find explanations linked to current source and tracked work. The bundled documentation/Carbon capability requires no external plugin; generation runs on demand.

# Governed project knowledge

## Describe intended application behavior

| Category | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| File | One source file and its responsibility |
| Rule | Invariant or condition; source and tests, or an explicit testGap |
| Feature | Observable capability; source and tests, or an explicit testGap |
| UI | Location, element, trigger, behavior and states; sources and tests or testGap |

Read contextory_catalog_get before related changes and page definitions, proposals and inventory independently. Generated entries begin as observations. A source graph describes possible relationships; it cannot approve a rule or infer intended interface behavior.

## Review pending items in Approvals

The persistent review alert, Approvals count and editor badge count pending change proposals only. Optional baseline review is collapsed initially; expand its summary with a click or keyboard to inspect observations. The chosen state is retained across refresh and navigation. These observations do not block work.

1. Open Approvals and read the agent’s explanation: what changes, why your approval is needed and how application behavior changes. Knowledge remains the browser for definitions, source coverage and immutable history.
2. Choose Approve or Reject without entering a comment. To ask for an update first, write your instructions and choose Request changes. A proposal with requested changes still blocks implementation; the agent revises that same proposal and waits for another decision.
3. Readable source snapshots refresh automatically and never grant approval or change the authored definition. Prior source hashes remain in history. Missing files still block approval. An edit during review refreshes the snapshot and asks you to inspect the latest item before retrying; no refresh button or refresh comment is required.

Saving, errors and success appear beside the controls. Failed responses preserve your instructions, and duplicate submissions are disabled. Switching to Knowledge and back preserves the draft; Knowledge filters do not hide approvals. Technical before/after definitions remain available through Definition history rather than filling the review card.

![Approvals showing the agent explanation, simple decisions and update instructions.](../assets/knowledge-preview.png)

Approvals rendered by the production webview with isolated example records; no real project approval was performed.

Human review in Approvals approves exact process/outcome changes and optional baselines. Agents use the leased auto-approval path for implementation maintenance/conflicts and cannot borrow human credentials. Pending proposals and stale affected approved definitions block completion. A compatible source refresh preserves the original human review and approved behavioral text; a changed file hash alone does not require changing the contract.

## Browse Knowledge independently

1. Choose Tools > Knowledge to browse current and historical definitions, their source/test links and history.
2. Expand Find definitions & coverage, then filter by text, path or category. File inventory stays available in this browser.
3. Choose Approvals to review pending items. Knowledge filters and pagination do not affect that queue; reviewed items disappear from Approvals and remain discoverable in Knowledge.

![Project knowledge browsing without approval forms.](../assets/knowledge-browser.png)

Knowledge browser using production UI and isolated fixture records.

## Bootstrap an existing project

Use the portable contextory-migrate skill within an authorized implementation request. contextory_catalog_migrate captures a bounded manifest and resumes by migrationId/cursor. Repeating the same operation/input returns the stored result. state=scanned means the file scan ended; it does not mean semantic review or approval is complete.

Inspect candidates against current source, callers, tests and historical decisions. Preserve contradictions, missing tests and unsupported runtime observations as explicit gaps. Reconcile files added after the captured manifest.

## Export stored documentation datasets

Discover and page project exports

```json
{ "section": "overview", "offset": 0, "limit": 20 }
```

Call contextory_project_export with the selected projectId. Page records, revisions, history, relationships, code_files, code_nodes, code_edges, code_imports, jobs, usage and artifacts until nextOffset=null. Keep sequence/snapshot, current versus historical state, provenance and source freshness. Artifacts use 400-character units; other datasets page rows.

This export excludes credentials, native conversations and numeric embedding vectors. Large responses may return artifact handles for further paging. A read-only export needs no implementation request.

## Choose approval by behavioral impact

Compatible maintenance needs no new human decision. Agents may auto-approve implementation conflicts too, with an explicit conflict assessment, rationale, source/test links and validation. Conflicts involving process rules or results, changed approved behavior, retirements and uncertain conflicts require human review before implementation. New observations have optional baseline review and do not trigger mandatory approval alerts.

Compatible source maintenance under the current lease

```json
{
  "action": "revise",
  "id": "KN-existing",
  "expectedRevision": 2,
  "specId": "SPEC-current",
  "leaseId": "current-lease",
  "operationId": "unique-operation-id",
  "compatibility": "preserved",
  "impact": "implementation",
  "autoApprove": true,
  "content": {
    "category": "feature",
    "title": "Stable greeting",
    "description": "Returns the configured greeting.",
    "sources": [
      {
        "path": "src/greeting.ts",
        "symbol": "greet"
      }
    ],
    "tests": [
      {
        "path": "tests/greeting.test.ts"
      }
    ]
  },
  "reason": "Function A replaced by B with the same results, errors and side effects; record the relevant validation."
}
```

Use compatibility=conflicting and impact=implementation only when the conflict cannot affect process rules or results. Preserve approved behavior descriptions and UI contracts exactly; file-purpose prose may be corrected for implementation changes. The server declines auto-approval for changed approved behavior, rule conflicts and process/outcome or unclassified related decisions. decisionIds retains links to earlier decisions. Auto-approval is an agent assessment, not proof of semantic equivalence or passing tests.

Every revision preserves the original definition, before/after source fingerprints, target revision, reason, spec, actor and review mode. Auto-approved changes have state=auto_approved; observed targets remain observed and approved behavioral targets retain their original human review. Knowledge displays agent maintenance provenance, and history, search, reports and project export retain the change. Test references never substitute for independent executed evidence.

Auto-approval preserves behavioral descriptions and UI contracts even on observed entries. When an approved file-purpose description changes, the new file observation is not attributed to the earlier human review; its approved baseline revision remains traceable.

## Wait before implementing a disputed change

Prepare the concrete proposal before editing disputed behavior. PreToolUse denies implementation tools while any project proposal is pending; Stop blocks completion. Read-only tools, catalog preparation, configured checks, questions/wait and lease renewal remain available. Contextory also rejects workflow mutations through its service, so direct MCP calls do not bypass the gate. Do not busy-poll or use another shell to proceed. Approval status is re-read on each event and survives service restarts; silence and timeout never approve anything.

Codex/Claude launchers emit structured deny/block responses plus exit code 2; Bob uses blocking stderr/exit code 2. A failed or obsolete approval-status contract blocks implementation/completion until recovery. Reload the service and native hook runtime together after upgrading. Native trust and actual hook delivery remain host-owned. Generic MCP has no native file-tool hook: the service enforces its own workflow, while agents must honor the wait for external edits. Hooks cannot intercept unreported changes, a human editor, or a client that never invokes them.

After approval, implement and validate the accepted behavior. After rejection, retain or restore the established behavior and validate it. Superseding process/outcome or unclassified decisions requires a human-approved proposal in the current spec, with the old decision in decisionIds and the exact replacement choice as content.description; pass its approvalId to contextory_decision_record. Only implementation-to-implementation decision conflicts auto-review.

## Trace a regression to a recorded change

1. Recover the affected feature/rule/UI contract, current source and last known working check or version. Record the symptom and reproducer as a finding.
2. Follow impact/path relationships and search by feature, path/symbol, catalog ID and earlier decisions. Page history and inspect exact before/after revisions, hashes, agent or human review, spec and evidence, including auto-approved changes.
3. Compare actual Git membership and the last working source. Reproduce candidate causes; static edges and recording intervals do not prove causation or shipped inclusion. Use a focused regression check and Git history/bisect when useful.
4. Link the confirmed finding/fix to the responsible change/spec/source with contextory_relationship_change. Record uncertainty if the cause is unproven; update catalog/docs and submit current independent evidence.

Auto-approval reduces interruptions, not traceability. All material changes still require indexed explanations and validation evidence so a later agent can investigate what changed and why.

## Return to the originating conversation

Attach the exact native session ID supplied by the Contextory hook. The project, provider, session and specification are saved on proposals and retained on claimed work after lease release. Approval, rejection and feedback are durable audit events returned only to that exact provider/session in the same project. An unknown origin remains unbound; the extension never guesses the active chat.

A trusted PreToolUse or Stop hook can wait up to four minutes for your decision and return it to that conversation. Approval releases the approved operation; rejection prevents the waiting operation, and feedback asks for a revised proposal. Expiry or service failure keeps the operation blocked. Responses remain queued until a matching hook receives them; transport acknowledgement does not prove the model acted on them. Hooks that are not trusted or a fully stopped client cannot resume automatically.

Use Reopen conversation on an approval or a specification’s Contract tab. Claude opens the saved session through the installed native extension command. Codex resumes that exact saved conversation in an interactive terminal with codex resume, because its documented extension commands expose neither targeted reopening nor targeted message submission. Bob, generic clients or an unavailable Claude command copy the saved session ID for manual history recovery. The native client owns history availability and permissions; no response is injected into an arbitrary chat.

[Claude session recovery contract](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#launch-a-vs-code-tab-from-other-tools)

[Documented Codex extension commands](https://developers.openai.com/codex/ide/commands)

# Project documentation

## Find an explanation

Contextory includes project documentation as an optional capability. The software-documentation 1.0.1 runtime, its authoring/update/source-comment/integration playbooks and the complete Carbon 1.0.0 module ship in the extension and CLI. Local fonts, tokens, templates and references need no separate plugin installation. Reading explanations works without Python; generation uses Python 3.11+ configured by contextory.pythonExecutable.

1. Choose Tools > Documentation. Search for a feature or behavior, optionally filter by source path, and choose English or Portuguese.
2. Read the explanation, stable page/section ID, source links and freshness badge. A draft, an unknown baseline and a stale explanation still need review; documentation never grants approval to a requirement.
3. From Architecture, choose Explain this area for the current source scope. In a request, expand Brief & actions and choose Related documentation to find sections linked to the request or its descendant records. Reference codebases remain a separate read-only source scope.

![Documentation search, English and Portuguese selection, stale explanation and source/record links.](../assets/documentation-browser.png)

Production documentation browser with isolated fixture explanations and explicit stale-source state.

## Author and build with your agent

1. Ask the agent to use contextory-documentation. It reads current source, catalog and the relevant exported Contextory datasets with their project identity and approval/history provenance.
2. Map the project and author substantive paired English/pt-BR explanations in .documentation/project.json. The bundled init operation creates a draft, not finished documentation. Preserve existing content, translations, IDs, URLs and assets.
3. Use contextory_docs_run for map/init/validate/build/integrations/migrate/readme/Pages operations and poll the returned job. Generation runs on demand and cannot gate service startup. Mutating operations require the agent’s current specification lease.
4. Review the generated responsive Carbon site, both locales, local search, examples, native source comments and coverage gaps. Consumer bundles include their own read-only documentation MCP and installer. Do not claim complete behavior coverage from file counts or a passed build.

The generator creates schema 2 Carbon sites, and retrieval also reads schema 1. Migration previews by default, creates a backup on apply and leaves migrated content in draft for review. Contextory’s own schema-1 site build remains separately pinned; this feature does not upgrade that corpus.

## Connect explanations to changes

After comparing a section with current sources, the agent uses contextory_docs_link with its page/section IDs, current corpus fingerprint, local record IDs and a reason. Contextory retains citation hashes, record revisions, semantic fingerprints and an audit trail of before/after associations. It stores these observed links in the selected project’s ledger; it does not inject private ledger history into public HTML.

Changed text/citations, changed or missing cited files and meaningful changes to linked records mark a section stale. Lease renewal alone does not invalidate the explanation. Current-project code context includes bounded relevant explanations when its token budget permits. Source definitions, generated architecture, authored explanations, historical decisions and human-approved requirements retain different authority.

Expand Keep documentation current for source mapping or validation. A successful runtime job can return valid=false, shown as needs review. Large results are retained as JSON artifacts and can be paged through project export. Exact operation retries recover the same job; failed/interrupted mutations are never replayed automatically.

## Publish explicitly and verify

Implementing documentation does not publish a connected project. With publication authorization, inspect pages_plan, select the intended remote, then run pages_publish with publish=true and the current lease. Verify pages_status against the actual live artifact. The bundled upstream publisher preserves orphan gh-pages history and rejects foreign branch replacement. GitHub CLI authentication/network/Pages availability remain environmental requirements.

Missing Python affects generator jobs only. Configure its executable and start a new operation after inspecting any partial files. A failed or unavailable documentation corpus does not block source context or the service. Human approvals remain in Approvals, and references never grant writes into another project.

# Project versions and releases

## Inspect repository-wide version history

Versions belongs to the whole repository, independently of requests, specs and leases. While the service runs, it observes Git and records exact commit membership for releases and unreleased changes. Read contextory_version_get or the Versions view and page commits and semantic records separately. Local tag observation does not prove remote publication.

![Project versions and release details in the editor Panel.](../assets/panel-versions.png)

Versions captured from the application.

## Prepare, apply and publish separately

1. Prepare a concrete release plan: inspect proposed version, HEAD, changed version files and changelog. Preparation does not edit source.
2. With authorization for the release, apply the reviewed plan to create its version commit and annotated local tag. Resolve stale plans or unrelated dirty changes before applying.
3. Publish the exact tag as a separate action using the configured Git remote and authentication. Verify remote state. Local application alone does not publish extension packages, releases or the documentation site.
4. After an uncertain result, recover the owned operation with its original operation ID/input. Never force or replace an existing tag. Cancel only an untouched plan.

Inspect and prepare; use returned IDs/revisions for later actions

```powershell
node dist/contextory.mjs versions
node dist/contextory.mjs release-prepare minor --operation prepare-unique-id
node dist/contextory.mjs versions REL-ID --offset 0 --limit 20
```

> Implementing software or rewriting documentation does not authorize releasing the repository. Release publication and a live editor installation remain separate user actions.

## Configure version adapters

contextory.release.json supports schemaVersion, initialVersion, tagPrefix, remote, optional branch, changelogPath and versionFiles. JSON adapters select key paths; text adapters use bounded prefix/suffix replacements. Use repository-relative ordinary files. Plans bind the exact source/configuration state and preserve unrelated changes.

Semantic records associated between release cutoffs remain interval associations, not proof they shipped in a commit. Release revisions and history remain exportable.

- contextory.release.json

# Clients, CLI and integration

## Understand each client adapter

| Client | MCP configuration | Skills / hooks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | .codex/config.toml | .agents/skills; .codex/hooks.json |
| Claude Code | .mcp.json | .claude/skills; .claude/settings.local.json |
| IBM Bob | .bob/mcp.json | .bob/skills; .bob/settings.json |
| Generic MCP | .contextory/mcp.json | .contextory/skills export; no hooks |

Connect through the extension commands. Contextory writes owned workspace-local entries and preserves unrelated settings. Malformed, linked or unowned conflicts fail without replacement. Native clients retain authentication, model selection, editing, permissions and trust. Hooks supply lifecycle reminders, metadata and pending approval decisions.

Native hooks enforce pending approval decisions before implementation and Stop, in addition to lifecycle reminders and normalized metadata. Agents may auto-approve only implementation maintenance/conflicts; process/outcome conflicts wait for human Approvals. Enforcement requires the host to trust and invoke the updated hooks.

## Use another MCP client

1. Run Contextory: Export Generic MCP Connection in the selected project.
2. Import its server entry into your client and copy the exported codebase, workflow and migration skill folders into that client’s supported discovery location.
3. Approve/reload through that client and make a read-only workspace/context call. .contextory/skills is an export location, not universal automatic discovery.

![Contextory sidebar with request progress and native agent controls.](../assets/companion-sidebar.png)

Contextory sidebar captured from the application; records are examples.

## Run without an editor

Packaged standalone commands

```powershell
node dist/contextory.mjs help
node dist/contextory.mjs index --root C:/Projects/Checkout
node dist/contextory.mjs context "payment retries" --root C:/Projects/Checkout --budget 3000
node dist/contextory.mjs mcp --root C:/Projects/Checkout
```

Use Node.js 24+ with the packaged dist directory. For stdio MCP configure node with arguments ["/absolute/path/dist/contextory.mjs", "mcp", "--root", "/absolute/project"]. The server remains alive until EOF/signals. Source inspection parses project files and does not execute them; configured checks execute only when explicitly requested.

> Standalone records default to <root>/.contextory-local/service and form a separate ledger. To share editor records, use --descriptor with the generic descriptor exported by the running editor and the matching --root. Back up whichever ledger you actually use.

## Install optional documentation guidance

The generated .documentation/integrations/contextory bundle contains this bilingual documentation snapshot, use/develop guidance and a read-only query MCP. It is separate from Contextory’s operational MCP and its codebase/workflow/migration skills.

Preview explicit installation into a chosen consumer workspace

```powershell
python .documentation/integrations/contextory/install.py --workspace C:/Projects/Consumer --client codex --dry-run
```

Remove --dry-run only for the explicitly selected consumer project. Supported clients are codex, claude and bob. Installing the extension or importing a package does not silently activate this optional documentation integration. Its queries read the installed snapshot; they do not control Contextory.

# Limits and compatibility

## Supported and unqualified environments

The qualified preview uses Windows, trusted local folders, Node.js 24+, VS Code 1.96+ or IBM Bob, and at most 16 non-nested workspace projects. Remote/virtual workspaces, other operating systems, arbitrary monorepo scale and authenticated end-to-end conversations in every native agent are not qualified.

## Source and flow analysis boundaries

Default interactive flow uses five call hops, 150 nodes, 300 edges and a two-second budget. Python flow scanning is bounded to 500 files, 512 KiB per file and 12 MiB total. Frontiers, cycles, unresolved targets and size/time boundaries remain visible. Expand or retrace to continue.

TypeScript and Python extraction is static. Dynamic dispatch, generated code, external dependencies and framework runtime behavior may not resolve. Other flow languages rely on available editor call hierarchy and do not automatically receive branch extraction. Saved graph results and unsaved flow overlays have different freshness rules.

## Recovery, revisions and concurrency

One active implementation lease owns each specification. Reread a record after a revision conflict; do not retry changed input with an old operation ID. Reuse exact operation/input only after an uncertain result. Cross-project creation is recoverable and may partially succeed; it is not an atomic transaction.

An unavailable source, stale Graphify import, missing independent check, pending Knowledge proposal or unresolved blocking finding stays an explicit limitation or completion blocker. Native permissions remain in force.

# Runtime architecture

## Follow the process boundaries

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Native agent | Conversation, model, sign-in, editing and native permissions |
| Editor extension and webviews | Trusted workspace setup, UI, source navigation and live theme integration |
| Isolated Node service | Role-scoped tools, workflow enforcement, ledger, search, checks and release observation |
| Analysis workers / Python parser | Bounded static extraction outside the Extension Host; no workspace module imports |
| SQLite storage | Authoritative records/revisions/artifacts and rebuildable graph/search projections |

Native MCP proxies connect to private local service descriptors. Hooks provide bounded lifecycle reminders and normalized metadata. Native/headless MCP, briefs and hooks share runtime guidance; provider-specific configuration remains in explicit adapters.

Native hooks enforce pending approval decisions before implementation and Stop, in addition to lifecycle reminders and normalized metadata. Agents may auto-approve only implementation maintenance/conflicts; process/outcome conflicts wait for human Approvals. Enforcement requires the host to trust and invoke the updated hooks.

## Preserve authoritative records

Requests, contracts, immutable revisions, decisions, check evidence, outcomes, Knowledge definitions and release records are authoritative project history. The source graph and lexical/vector indexes are projections that can be rebuilt. Rebuilding source analysis must not erase workflow history.

Each workspace project owns its ledger, sessions, leases, checks, references and releases. Cross-project routing validates current editor membership and preserves the caller’s role. A reference repository has an isolated read-only projection inside its owning project.

## Understand privacy and authority

Contextory stores concise project explanations and observed metadata rather than native chat transcripts. Check output and indexed project content are retained locally. Human Knowledge review is enforced by service roles, but a process with unrestricted local filesystem access is not isolated from service credentials or SQLite by this design.

[Read storage and settings details](reference.md)

# Settings, commands and storage

## Workspace settings

| Setting | Default | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| contextory.autoConnect | true | Prepare detected agent bridges; pause preserves existing connections |
| contextory.startupAgent | auto | auto, last-used, codex, claude, bob or none |
| contextory.restartAfterSetup | prompt | prompt, automatic or never after changed MCP/hooks/runtime |
| contextory.nodeExecutable | node | Machine-level Node.js 24+ executable |
| contextory.pythonExecutable | python | Machine-level Python 3.10+ executable for analysis |
| contextory.flowDepth | 5 | Call-hop depth, 0–12 |
| contextory.checks | [] | Up to 256 named executable/argument-array recipes; invalid changes retain the connection and last valid list |

## Editor commands

Use the Command Palette for connection setup/recovery, architecture, flow, indexing, semantic preparation, reports and generic MCP export. The exact command IDs/titles and configuration defaults are declared in package.json; inspect them when adapting automation to a newer version.

[Connection and check setup](quickstart.md)

[Tool signatures and input schemas](api.md)

## Storage and backups

Editor records, revisions, audit events, artifacts and service credentials live in editor-managed global storage for contextory-local.contextory-workspace, namespaced by canonical project path. Exact locations depend on the editor/profile. Moving a project changes its identity in this preview. Agent bridge configuration and portable skills live in the workspace.

Standalone mode defaults to <root>/.contextory-local/service unless --storage or a matching live editor --descriptor is provided. This is authoritative storage, not just a disposable build cache. Back it up when using headless mode.

1. Close clients for the project and let the editor service stop after its approximately 65-second grace period.
2. Copy the relevant editor-managed project storage or headless service directory as a consistent backup.
3. Retain native provider credentials separately. Do not edit SQLite or service descriptors to bypass workflow or review controls.

## Read this documentation’s coverage correctly

The bilingual corpus is the source of the human pages, Markdown and LLM exports. Its ownership roots cover the documentation build scripts; Contextory source and tests are cited as hash-bound supporting evidence. Application function/class docstrings were not rewritten. The generated source-symbol appendix therefore documents the build tooling, while the MCP API page documents the product’s public tool contracts.

The historical documentation rewrite used native inspection while Contextory was unavailable. The 0.8.0 delivery recovered the original service ledger and inspected current source and tracked work. Observed catalog definitions are not human-approved requirements. See the review record for scope and evidence limits.

# Frequently asked questions

## Does Contextory replace my chat or model?

No. Keep using your native agent. Contextory supplies shared project records and tools; conversation history, sign-in, model selection and editing stay with the client.

## Do I need Python or a model download?

Node.js 24+ is required. Python 3.10+ is needed only for Python analysis. Local semantic retrieval is optional; lexical/structural retrieval works without an embedding download.

## Does a code question need a tracked request?

Read-only source questions and documentation exports do not. Authorized implementation uses requests, milestones, criteria, a session/lease and independent evidence before explicit completion.

## Why is a submitted specification still open?

Outcome submission records the explanation. The agent must separately request completion with the returned current revision. Missing checks, stale evidence, dependencies, blocking findings and catalog proposals can prevent completion.

## Does a green agent light prove authentication?

It proves observed MCP traffic for that configured provider in this service instance. It does not prove model sign-in or execution of every hook. Use native trust controls and connection diagnostics for more detail.

## Can an agent approve its own Knowledge definition?

Compatible maintenance needs no new human decision. Agents may auto-approve implementation conflicts too, with an explicit conflict assessment, rationale, source/test links and validation. Conflicts involving process rules or results, changed approved behavior, retirements and uncertain conflicts require human review before implementation. New observations have optional baseline review and do not trigger mandatory approval alerts.

## Is a graph or linked test execution evidence?

No. Static extraction and test references indicate possible relationships. Verification requires actual current check results with their provenance and source/contract/attempt fingerprints.

## Does Contextory follow VS Code's language?

Yes. The built-in interface supports English and Brazilian Portuguese using vscode.env.language, with English fallback for other locales. Agents receive the project uiLanguage and must author new interface entries in that language. Historical/user content and code are preserved; documentation retains its English/pt-BR pair.

# Troubleshooting and recovery

## Recover service and native connections

| Symptom | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Service unavailable | Keep the project editor open, check Node 24+ in its PATH, set contextory.nodeExecutable if needed and inspect Output > Contextory |
| Analysis or connection disabled | Trust a supported local workspace; avoid virtual/remote or nested project roots |
| Gray agent light | Hover for configuration/traffic state, click to retry setup, review native MCP/hook trust and make a read-only call |
| Tools missing in an old chat | Restart agent extensions, reload the native MCP connection and reopen the chat as required by that client |
| Hooks remain unobserved | Rebuild once, inspect repaired files, then check native trust and trigger a supported lifecycle event; unchanged files are not execution evidence |
| Unowned or malformed configuration | Resolve the concrete conflict; registration preserves unowned entries and refuses linked paths |
| Older service after an upgrade | Follow the mismatch message; close project editors for about 65 seconds before reopening when requested |

[Connection and hook recovery walkthrough](user-guide.md)

## Automatic recovery and request timeouts

The editor probes service health every 20 seconds with a five-second timeout. Lost streams, including clean closure, trigger reconnection after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and at most 30 seconds. The view labels retained data and offers Retry now. Recovery never replays failed mutations.

REQUEST_TIMEOUT means an operation exceeded its request budget; it does not establish SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE. Ordinary tools allow 120 seconds and release operations have their separate five-minute budget. For an uncertain mutation response, recover with the exact original operation ID and input.

For the former Configure at most 30 check recipes error, upgrade to 0.8.0: up to 256 recipes are supported. Fix duplicate IDs or malformed recipes through Fix check settings. Configuration errors retain the service and its last valid recipes.

Rebuild hooks writes managed files immediately. Changed repairs follow contextory.restartAfterSetup: prompt, automatic or never. The installed Codex extension exposes no public hook-refresh command; Contextory cannot grant native trust or guarantee immediate reload inside a running chat. Review /hooks in that session, keep workspace path casing consistent and reopen the chat after restarting extensions when required.

## Recover source results and completion

| Symptom | Action |
| --- | --- |
| An item remains pending in Approvals | Read the inline error. Sources refresh automatically; no comment is needed. Restore missing files or ask the agent to correct references. Request changes for an outdated target or incomplete explanation; the agent revises the proposal and waits again. If a reply is queued, resume the linked conversation and check native hook trust. |
| Python flow fails | Check Python 3.10+ and contextory.pythonExecutable; use an absolute executable path if needed |
| Unexpected source root | Set projectId/codebaseId explicitly and focus the intended editor symbol before tracing |
| Source search seems stale | Re-query saved source; refresh an empty/failed index, inspect exclusions and regenerate/re-import stale Graphify data |
| Semantic search unavailable | Prepare the optional local runtime and index, or use lexical/hybrid fallback |
| Spec stays submitted | Poll check jobs, resolve blockers and stale evidence, submit every criterion mapping, then explicitly complete using the returned revision |
| Cross-project group incomplete | Restore missing/offline workspace members and recover missing branches on the original owner; verify each local request |

## Report a reproducible issue

Include Contextory version, editor/version, Node/Python versions, exact error text and reproduction steps. Remove credentials, private descriptors, tokens and project-private records before sharing logs. Preserve current coverage and unverified limits.

[Open the issue tracker](https://github.com/igormicadei/Contextory/issues)

# Write useful implementation outcomes

## Explain what changed and why

- Identify the request/spec, current revision and original user intent. Describe the resulting behavior with source references.
- Record findings with impact, resolution and why the fix works. Explicitly say when there were no findings.
- Explain material choices, alternatives and consequences. Distinguish an agent decision from a human requirement.
- Map every current criterion exactly once to current evidence. Retain actual command/job result, origin, skips and limits.
- Include catalog.recordIds and catalog.explanation when the catalog exists. Explain updated definitions or unchanged behavior.

## Submit and explicitly complete

1. Finish source/configuration edits before final independent checks. Later changes can invalidate evidence.
2. Submit contextory_outcome_submit with the current revision, evidence mappings, report/changelog text and limitations.
3. Use contextory_spec_change action=complete with the returned revision and a new operationId. Confirm state=completed and export the request report.

![Request list beside the selected specification.](../assets/panel-requests.png)

Requests in a horizontal editor Panel.

The snapshot hashes the complete contents of manifest files using 1 MiB read chunks. Files larger than 20 MiB remain included; fixtures do not need to be removed to run checks. If a file changes size, modification/metadata timestamps, identity or type during the read, capture is rejected with STALE_SOURCE. Before/after command snapshot comparison and independent-evidence requirements remain active.

## Sources

- src/contracts/tools.ts
- src/core/workflow.ts
- src/core/report.ts
- tests/core/workflow.test.ts
- src/verification/workspace.ts

# Build, document and contribute

## Set up development

Build and run project checks

```powershell
npm ci
npx playwright install chromium
npm run check
```

Use Node.js 24+, npm and Python 3.10+ for analysis tests. npm run check runs portable-skill drift checks, TypeScript, production build, backend tests and UI tests. Optional real-model tests need the separately prepared embedding runtime. Host qualification remains separate.

## Find the owning subsystem

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| src/codebase | Source projection, extractors, freshness and queries |
| src/service, src/contracts, src/core, src/storage | Service/tool contracts, tracked work and authoritative ledger |
| src/knowledge, src/analysis, src/editor | Governed memory, flow analysis and editor integration |
| src/releases | Git observation, release plans, adapters and recoverable tags |
| src/providers/clients.ts, src/agents/instructions.ts | Client capabilities and shared portable guidance |
| src/webview, media, tests | User interfaces, assets and backend/UI/host validation |

Edit canonical portable skills in skills/, then run npm run skills:sync. Do not edit generated provider skill-content or client copies independently. Preserve unrelated source and client configuration.

## Maintain the default documentation site

Documentation workflow

```powershell
npm run docs:map
npm run docs:validate
npm run docs:build
npm run docs:integrations
npm run docs:preview
```

Edit .documentation/project.json: page/section IDs are shared by en and pt-BR. Use source-backed plain-text blocks, translated examples/captions/alt text and actual application screenshots. The vendored software-documentation runtime renders its unchanged Carbon shell, local search, responsive navigation, Markdown, llms.txt and corpus/API exports. Python 3.11+ is required for documentation tooling.

The published root opens the default English overview directly, without a language chooser. Language switching remains available in each page header.

After reviewing changed source, set audit.reviewedSourceFingerprint to the current docs:map value. Builds refuse stale reviews; the build never approves source changes automatically. Use docs:migrate to inspect source drift. It previews supported versioned migration and refuses unknown schemas.

Generated output is .documentation/site/. The managed manifest detects stale inputs and protects unrelated output files. Existing URLs are kept by .documentation/redirects.json; old fragments remain usable on compatibility pages. Original English guides, plans, skills and release records are preserved under .documentation/legacy and published as archive downloads. Current guides under docs/ are managed English exports of the same corpus.

The existing documentation workflow builds relevant main-branch changes and updates gh-pages. A local build does not publish it. Review current hashes and the orphan branch history before any authorized deployment, then verify the live artifact. README links describe the intended site URL until deployment is verified.

## Package and qualify changes

Build the local distributable

```powershell
npm run package:vsix
```

Packaging refreshes the versioned VSIX and checksum but does not publish, change a version or install into a live editor. Changes to MCP transport/registration need headless/service/registration integration checks. Run real editor-host smoke checks for host changes and record authenticated native chat limitations accurately.

[Review qualification evidence](validation.md)

## Maintain interface translations safely

Use package.nls.json and package.nls.pt-br.json for extension contributions; keep command IDs and setting keys unchanged. Source-owned webview/host messages use tx for controlled labels or the ui template tag for HTML and interpolated messages. The helper translates the static skeleton before substituting values. Do not apply translation to stored record titles, descriptions, reasons, code or paths. Machine IDs, selectors, CSS classes and SVG coordinates are not localized.

Translate the label, preserve the record

```typescript
import { ui } from "../i18n";
// escape preserves the existing HTML-escaping boundary.
return ui`<h1>Requests</h1><p>${escape(record.title)}</p>`;
```

Add the matching Portuguese message to src/i18n/pt-BR.json and preserve numbered numbered substitution markers. npm run i18n:check extracts declared messages and checks Portuguese coverage, substitution marker parity and manifest catalogs; npm run check includes it. New UI-facing agent prose follows contextory_context_get.uiLanguage. English source keys and protocol/schema identifiers remain stable. Activity presentation separates the localized action from the untouched record subject.

# Validation and evidence boundaries

## Match each check to its claim

| Check | Establishes |
| --- | --- |
| npm run check | Skill bundle consistency, types, production build, backend and browser UI regression checks |
| Service/headless/registration integration | Tool contracts, transport, role isolation, setup ownership and tracked workflow scenarios |
| Editor-host smoke checks | Actual packaged activation, commands, service, configuration and persistence in isolated profiles |
| docs:validate and docs:build | Bilingual corpus structure, cited source hashes, images, generated exports and local links/anchors |
| Documentation browser review | Desktop/mobile layout, locale parity, navigation, search and screenshot rendering for the reviewed build |

## Separate earlier qualification from this rewrite

The original validation record and release notes are preserved as historical downloads. Their passing results describe the code/artifacts tested at that time. They are not automatically new test executions for this documentation rewrite. The rewrite’s concrete commands/results belong in .documentation/REVIEW.md.

Existing screenshots are application captures with example records. The documentation build validates file presence and bilingual captions/alt text. Browser review verifies rendering; it does not recreate an authenticated native-agent conversation.

## Keep remaining gaps explicit

The earlier documentation rewrite recorded an unavailable service; the 0.8.0 delivery recovered the original project ledger and uses tracked release checks. Catalog entries remain observations until human review. Native trust, authenticated agent chats, dynamic/static-analysis gaps, remote workspaces and other operating systems retain their own qualification limits.

## Approval policy and traceability validation

Disposable integration fixtures exercise compatible function replacement with the same result, approved-contract preservation, audited implementation conflicts, process/outcome/rule guards, exact decision supersession approval, source staleness, service-side bypass rejection, restart persistence and real packaged hook processes for Codex/Claude/Bob. Browser fixtures verify optional observations, required review counts and visible agent provenance. These tests establish launcher/service contracts; they do not automate authenticated native conversations, hook trust or interception of unreported edits.

## English and Portuguese localization checks

Checks cover locale normalization/fallback, static message and manifest coverage, substitution marker preservation, untouched dynamic records/code/attributes, webview language/CSP, project-scoped authenticated configuration, persisted context/hook instructions, English regressions and Portuguese navigation/accessibility/layout in sidebar, short panel and standalone workbenches. The isolated editor smoke compares the project context with the actual vscode.env.language. Raw external diagnostics are allowed to retain their source language.

# MCP API reference

## Read the advertised contract

Contextory 0.11.0 defines 39 tools. The following Zod schema excerpts were extracted with the TypeScript parser from the saved source without executing application code. They preserve required/optional/default/range semantics. The running MCP tools/list response is authoritative for the installed client version. contextory_catalog_review is human-UI-only even if its contract is visible.

Every tool additionally accepts optional projectId and workspaceId. Omitted/current project scope stays on that server’s project. Source tools additionally accept optional codebaseId where their schema/advertised contract permits it. Lines/characters in product tool source references are zero-based; documentation citation lines are one-based.

Shared schema aliases

```typescript
const id = z.string().min(1).max(160);
const text = z.string().min(1).max(12000);
const operationId = z.string().min(8).max(160);
const expectedRevision = z.number().int().positive().optional();
const source = z.object({
  path: z.string().min(1).max(2000),
  line: z.number().int().nonnegative().optional(),
  character: z.number().int().nonnegative().optional(),
  symbol: z.string().max(500).optional(),
});
const lease = { specId: id, leaseId: id };
const category = z.enum(["file", "rule", "feature", "ui"]);
export const catalogContent = z
  .object({
    category,
    title: z.string().trim().min(1).max(300),
    description: text,
    sources: z.array(source).min(1).max(30),
    tests: z.array(source).max(30).default([]),
    testGap: z.string().trim().min(1).max(2000).optional(),
    ui: z
      .object({
        location: text,
        element: text,
        trigger: text,
        behavior: text,
        states: text,
      })
      .optional(),
  })
  .superRefine((p, ctx) => {
    if (p.category === "file" && p.sources.length !== 1)
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: "custom",
        message: "A file entry describes exactly one source file.",
      });
    if (p.category === "ui" && !p.ui)
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: "custom",
        message:
          "UI contracts need location, element, trigger, behavior and states.",
      });
    if (p.category !== "file" && !p.tests.length && !p.testGap)
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: "custom",
        message: "Behavior needs test links or an explicit testGap.",
      });
  });
const limits = z
  .object({
    callDepth: z.number().int().min(0).max(12).optional(),
    nodes: z.number().int().min(5).max(500).optional(),
    edges: z.number().int().min(5).max(1000).optional(),
    targetsPerCall: z.number().int().min(1).max(30).optional(),
    timeoutMs: z.number().int().min(100).max(10000).optional(),
  })
  .optional();

```

## Revisions, retries and completion

Read a record before editing. Existing records require current expectedRevision. Use a fresh operationId (8–160 characters) for a new mutation; retry uncertain work only with its exact original input/ID. Implementation writes require the attached session’s active spec lease except documented setup/release operations. Native permissions still apply.

[Evidence and completion sequence](outcomes.md)

    })
```

## Catalog get

      pendingOnly: z.boolean().default(false),
      offset: z.number().int().nonnegative().default(0),
      limit: z.number().int().min(1).max(50).default(20),
    })
```

## Catalog change

Compatible maintenance needs no new human decision. Agents may auto-approve implementation conflicts too, with an explicit conflict assessment, rationale, source/test links and validation. Conflicts involving process rules or results, changed approved behavior, retirements and uncertain conflicts require human review before implementation. New observations have optional baseline review and do not trigger mandatory approval alerts.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:219

```typescript
z.object({
      operationId,
      ...lease,
      action: z.enum(["create", "revise", "retire"]),
      id: id.optional(),
      expectedRevision,
      content: catalogContent.optional(),
      reason: text.trim().min(1),
      migrationId: id.optional(),
      compatibility: z
        .enum(["preserved", "changed", "conflicting", "unknown"])
        .default("unknown"),
      impact: z
        .enum(["implementation", "process", "outcome", "unknown"])
        .default("unknown"),
      autoApprove: z.boolean().default(false),
      decisionIds: z.array(id).max(30).default([]),
      explanation: z
        .object({
          change: text.trim().min(1),
          approvalReason: text.trim().min(1),
          behavior: text.trim().min(1),
        })
        .optional(),
    })
```

## Catalog review

Human UI only. Approve/reject an exact revision without a required comment, or send feedback with update instructions. Source snapshots refresh automatically without approval. The legacy refresh action remains compatible. Requested changes keep implementation blocked until the agent revises the proposal and receives another decision.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:248

```typescript
z
      .object({
        operationId,
        id,
        expectedRevision: z.number().int().positive(),
        action: z.enum(["approve", "reject", "feedback", "refresh"]),
        reason: z.string().max(12000).trim().default(""),
      })
      .refine((p) => p.action !== "feedback" || p.reason.length > 0, {
        message: "Describe the update you want the agent to make.",
        path: ["reason"],
      })
```

## Decision record

Record impact and concise decision rationale. Implementation-to-implementation supersession auto-reviews; process/outcome or unclassified conflicts require the exact human-approved proposal approvalId with matching decisionIds and replacement description before implementation. Prior decisions retain their original content and supersedes links across specs.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:381

```typescript
z.object({
      operationId,
      ...lease,
      title: z.string().min(1).max(300),
      choice: text,
      rationale: text,
      alternatives: z.string().max(12000).default("None material"),
      consequences: text,
      supersedes: id.optional(),
      impact: z
        .enum(["implementation", "process", "outcome", "unknown"])
        .default("unknown"),
      approvalId: id.optional(),
      sources: z.array(source).max(30).default([]),
    })
```

## Outcome submit

Submit criterion evidence and a durable report; a separate complete action is still required.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:423

```typescript
z.object({
      operationId,
      ...lease,
      expectedRevision: z.number().int().positive(),
      summary: text,
      issuesSummary: text,
      decisionsSummary: text,
      limitations: text,
      report: text,
      changelog: z.string().min(1).max(2000),
      catalog: z
        .object({ recordIds: z.array(id).max(200), explanation: text })
        .optional(),
      criteria: z
        .array(
          z.object({
            criterionId: id,
            evidenceIds: z.array(id).min(1).max(30),
          }),
        )
        .min(1)
        .max(50),
      commits: z
        .array(z.string().regex(/^[a-f0-9]{40,64}$/))
        .max(100)
        .default([]),
    })
```

## Code path get

Explain a bounded indexed path between two source/record roots.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:483

```typescript
z.object({
      codebaseId: id.optional(),
      from: z.string().min(1).max(2500),
      to: z.string().min(1).max(2500),
      direction: z.enum(["forward", "both"]).default("both"),
      maxDepth: z.number().int().min(1).max(10).default(6),
    })
```

## Codebase change

Register or detach an authorized local reference; source files remain untouched.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:507

```typescript
z
      .object({
        operationId,
        action: z.enum(["add", "remove"]),
        root: z.string().min(1).max(2000).optional(),
        name: z.string().trim().min(1).max(100).optional(),
        codebaseId: id.optional(),
      })
      .refine(
        (p) => (p.action === "add" ? Boolean(p.root) : Boolean(p.codebaseId)),
        "Add requires root; remove requires codebaseId.",
      )
```

## Run bundled documentation operations

Queue any upstream documentation operation on demand; mutating operations need a lease and Pages publication needs explicit authorization plus publish=true. Poll the durable job and inspect its result.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:82

```typescript
z.object({
      operationId,
      action: z.enum([
        "map",
        "init",
        "validate",
        "build",
        "integrations",
        "migrate",
        "readme",
        "pages_plan",
        "pages_publish",
        "pages_status",
      ]),
      specId: id.optional(),
      leaseId: id.optional(),
      name: z.string().trim().min(1).max(300).optional(),
      kind: z.enum(["application", "library", "plugin"]).optional(),
      sourceRoots: z
        .array(z.string().min(1).max(2000))
        .min(1)
        .max(30)
        .optional(),
      apply: z.boolean().default(false),
      siteUrl: z.string().max(2000).optional(),
      remote: z.string().max(300).optional(),
      publish: z.boolean().default(false),
      offset: z.number().int().nonnegative().default(0),
      limit: z.number().int().min(1).max(1000).default(100),
    })
```
